Password.//: Length is the only composition requirement (ASVS 6.2.5). A digit, an uppercase letter and a symbol were demanded and are no longer: those rules refused long passphrases and accepted Password1!, so what they really selected for was the weakest password that satisfied them. The breached-password list below does the job they were meant to do.

CommonPasswords.//: Refuses passwords known from credential breaches (ASVS 6.2.4) — 19,179 entries embedded in PixSmith.Authorization.Services. ListPath reads a file instead, one password per line, to supply a larger list without a rebuild; a missing or empty list fails startup rather than quietly accepting everything. Enabled:false is a deliberate weakening now that the composition rules are off.

M2MClient.//: ClientSecret is deliberately absent. A client secret committed to the repository is a known secret, so it is supplied per environment instead — dotnet user-secrets locally, .env for the debug stack, the secret store in staging and production. Startup fails without it.

TenantEnforcement.//: Clients exempt from the tenancy membership/subscription checks because they administer the auth server itself rather than a company's data. Keep this list short; never add a customer-facing client. See docs/MULTI-TENANCY.md.

RateLimiting.//: Request-rate limits on the endpoints that accept credentials, partitioned by client IP. Identity's lockout caps failures per account; this is what bounds credential stuffing across many accounts and CPU exhaustion through the password hasher. Set Enabled to false only with another limiter in front.

RefreshTokens.//: AbsoluteLifetimeSeconds is the hard cap on a chain of refresh tokens, counted from the original grant: once it runs out the refresh is refused and the user signs in again, however often they refreshed. SlidingLifetimeSeconds is the idle timeout for any one token; set it to 0 to pin every refresh token to the absolute deadline instead, which keeps exp identical across a refresh but gives up the idle timeout.

TenantProvisioning.//: Public keys ONLY. Private keys are held offline by named humans and never appear here or in the database. Populate Keys via user-secrets (dev) or the secret store (production) — an empty list means tenant provisioning is denied, which is the intended fail-closed default.
